slides.title: Welcome to HTML Links & Navigation
slides.content:
# Links & Navigation 🔗

Hyperlinks are the core defining feature of the World Wide Web, allowing documents to connect across servers, domains, and pages.

## What you'll master:
- ⚓ **The Anchor Tag (`<a>`)** - Anatomy and the `href` attribute
- 🌐 **Absolute vs Relative URLs** - Root-relative, folder paths, and external destinations
- 🎯 **Link Targets & Security** - `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`
- 📍 **Fragment Identifiers** - Internal page jump links (`#id`)
- ✉️ **Protocol Links** - `mailto:`, `tel:`, and file downloads
- 🧭 **Accessible Navigation Menus** - Building responsive navbars and breadcrumbs

slides.title: The Anchor Element (<a>)
slides.content: # The Anchor Element (``) ⚓ The `` tag creates a hyperlink to another web page, file, email address, or internal section. ```html_not Visit Example Website ``` ## How It Works: - `href` (**H**ypertext **Ref**erence): Specifies the target destination URL. - The clickable anchor text goes between opening and closing tags. - Without an `href` attribute, the `` tag acts merely as a placeholder for a link.

slides.title: Absolute vs Relative URLs
slides.content: # Absolute vs Relative URLs 🌐 Understanding URLs is vital for correct site linking: ## 1. Absolute URLs: Full address including protocol and domain name. Required when linking to external websites: ```html_not Visit GitHub Profile ``` ## 2. Relative URLs: Path relative to the current file location on the same website: ```html_not About Us Read Article Back to Home Pricing Plans ```

slides.title: Link Targets: Opening in New Tabs
slides.content: # The `target` Attribute & Security 🎯 The `target` attribute specifies where to open the linked document: | Target Value | Behavior | | :--- | :--- | | `_self` | Default. Opens link in the same browser window/tab | | `_blank` | Opens link in a brand new tab or window | | `_parent` | Opens link in the parent frame | | `_top` | Opens link in the full body of the current window | ```html_not Search on Google (Opens New Tab) ``` > 🔒 **Critical Security Rule:** Whenever you use `target="_blank"`, you **must** add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to prevent the new page from accessing `window.opener` and hijacking your site!

slides.title: Internal Page Jumps (Fragment Identifiers)
slides.content:
# Internal Page Jumps (`#id`) 📍 Hyperlinks can navigate directly to a specific section on the same page using **fragment identifiers**. ```html_not Jump to FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Here are the answers...

``` When clicked, the browser automatically scrolls smoothly to the element with `id="faq-section"`.

slides.title: Smooth Scrolling with CSS
Special Protocol Links: Email & Phone
slides.content: # Email & Telephone Links ✉️📞 HTML links can launch the user's default email client or phone dialer. ## 1. Email Links (`mailto:`): ```html_not Contact Support ``` ## 2. Phone Call Links (`tel:`): On mobile devices, clicking a `tel:` link opens the phone dialer: ```html_not Call Us: (555) 123-4567 ``` ## 3. SMS Links (`sms:`): ```html_not Send SMS ```

slides.title: Download Links
slides.content: # The `download` Attribute 💾 The `download` attribute instructs the browser to download the linked file instead of navigating to it. ```html_not Download PDF Cheat Sheet Download Roadmap ``` > 💡 **Browser Rule:** The `download` attribute only works for same-origin URLs or files served with appropriate CORS headers.

slides.title: Breadcrumb Navigation
Accessible Link Text Best Practices
slides.content:
# Accessible Link Text Best Practices ♿

Screen reader users frequently navigate pages by listening to a generated list of all links on the page.

## Bad Link Text ❌:
- *"Click here"*
- *"Read more"*
- *"https://example.com/item/4019284"*

## Good Link Text ✅:
- *"Download the 2026 Web Development Roadmap (PDF)"*
- *"Read our complete guide to CSS Flexbox"*
- *"View Sarah Connor's GitHub profile"*

> 💡 **Self-Contained Rule:** Link text should always make sense completely out of context!

slides.title: Keyboard Navigation and Tabindex
slides.content:
# Keyboard Navigation & `tabindex` ⌨️

By default, all `<a>` tags with an `href` attribute are in the natural keyboard tab order (press Tab to navigate, Enter to activate).

## The `tabindex` Attribute:
- `tabindex="0"`: Inserts a non-interactive element (like a `<div>`) into the natural tab order.
- `tabindex="-1"`: Removes the element from the tab order, but allows programmatic focus with `.focus()`.
- `tabindex="1+"`: ❌ Avoid positive numbers! They distort the natural tab order and confuse users.

slides.title: Link Relationships with rel
slides.content:
# Advanced Link Relationships (`rel`) 🔗

The `rel` attribute defines the relationship between the current document and the linked resource:

- `rel="author"`: Links to author information.
- `rel="license"`: Links to copyright licensing terms.
- `rel="nofollow"`: Instructs search engines not to endorse or pass PageRank to the linked URL.
- `rel="prev"` / `rel="next"`: Indicates sequential pagination.
- `rel="canonical"`: Used in `<link>` tags in the head to prevent duplicate content penalties.

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Links & Navigation Complete! 🌟

You now command complete mastery over web hyperlinks and accessible navigation architecture!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **The Anchor Tag:** `<a>` with `href` links documents together.
- ✅ **Security:** Always pair `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- ✅ **Page Jumps:** Use fragment identifiers `#section-id` for smooth scrolling.
- ✅ **Special Protocols:** `mailto:` for email, `tel:` for calls, and `download` for saving files.
- ✅ **Accessibility:** Provide descriptive text and 'Skip to content' links.
